legend: VK news recommendation system daily selects interesting publications of one of n%%ZSMJ0%% disjoint categories for each user. Each publication belongs to exactly one category. For each category i%%ZSMJ1%% batch algorithm selects ai%%ZSMJ2%% publications.

The latest A/B test suggests that users are reading recommended publications more actively if each category has a different number of publications within daily recommendations. The targeted algorithm can find a single interesting publication of i%%ZSMJ3%%-th category within ti%%ZSMJ4%% seconds.

What is the minimum total time necessary to add publications to the result of batch algorithm execution, so all categories have a different number of publications? You can't remove publications recommended by the batch algorithm.
input: The first line of input consists of single integer n%%ZSMJ5%% — the number of news categories (1≤n≤200000%%ZSMJ6%%).
The second line of input consists of n%%ZSMJ7%% integers ai%%ZSMJ8%% — the number of publications of i%%ZSMJ9%%-th category selected by the batch algorithm (1≤ai≤109%%ZSMJ10%%).
The third line of input consists of n%%ZSMJ11%% integers ti%%ZSMJ12%% — time it takes for targeted algorithm to find one new publication of category i%%ZSMJ13%% (1≤ti≤105)%%ZSMJ14%%.
output: Print one integer — the minimal required time for the targeted algorithm to get rid of categories with the same size.
note: In the first example, it is possible to find three publications of the second type, which will take 6 seconds.
In the second example, all news categories contain a different number of publications.
